parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is a hostile parent framework plus the division's criminal bathroom law effective 1 July 2026 — the only such law reaching private businesses (gas stations, restaurants, hospitals), with up to one year's jail. This is a tier-1 universal exposure: every outed or outable visitor must use facilities, and using them congruently is a crime, with no working remedy (the suit is unresolved, and its outcome is unknown). The national layer compounds it: passports forced to birth sex, X markers ended, visa officers instructed to refuse on 'reasonable doubt' about sex with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, documented passport confiscations stranding travellers, and foreign governments issuing travel advisories after detentions. National custody records document hormone removal and sexual abuse. No organised sweeps of visitors or near-certain imprisonment are documented, keeping this above the 0.15 tier, but the criminal statute plus federal document hostility with thin recourse sits in the high-risk band, near the 0.25–0.35 boundary.

entry_documents.exposure: National passports/visas forced to birth sex; X markers ended; officers instructed to refuse on 'reasonable doubt' as to sex with possible lifetime fraud finding; documented passport confiscations stranding travellers; foreign advisories issued after detentions.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires all four elements and is not automatic; litigation against passport policy unresolved but pending.
entry_documents.interaction: A visitor's home documents can conflict with national entry processing, escalating to refusal or investigation at the border stage.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau adopted policies described as cutting hair and removing hormone medication; immigration custody documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans detainees. A visitor arrested under the bathroom offence enters this custody system.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State/province-level ruling (Sept 2024) permits hormone therapy in this state's prisons; 24-hour release documented in the one known arrest.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A facility complaint or arrest can move from local police into national immigration or corrections custody with documented harm.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division law criminalises restroom use congruent with identity in government buildings AND public-facing private businesses, up to one year jail; ~20 state/provinces bar facilities per identity in government buildings; 4 criminalise in some circumstances.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 state/provinces and capital district have no mapped ban; municipal protections cover ~40% of this division's population; suits pending.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The ban applies at every public-facing business the visitor enters daily — unavoidable, not occasional.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for minors banned in 27 state/provinces; national funding freeze and insurance-reimbursement proposals; this division requires medical professionals to disclose a trans minor's status to parents within three days.
care_services.protection: Not documented for adult visitors; state prescription availability noted only for prisoners.
care_services.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor enters a jurisdiction that mandates disclosure and criminalised facilitation at national level.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders frame trans people as 'mutilation' perpetrators and 'radical gender ideology' as extremism; counterterrorism strategy prioritises neutralising 'radically pro-transgender' groups; bathroom offence framed as protection from deceivers.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several orders blocked or enjoined; employment discrimination ruling remains; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing legitimises officer suspicion; the one documented arrest was treated as criminal trespass with handcuffing.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling with a minor: this division mandates disclosure of a trans minor's status to parents within three days; national EO directs prosecution of those facilitating a minor's transition; a prior bill would have imposed felony liability on parents seeking care abroad.
minors_guardians.protection: The felony-parent bill was blocked in the upper chamber; care-disclosure law, not prosecution, is the documented state measure.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardians risk both the child's outing and scrutiny of facilitation through state-mandated disclosure channels.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-specific violence data materially above the general homicide rate was identified; 37 state/provinces lacked gender-identity bias statutes as of 2019, so recourse is uneven.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crimes statute nationally; 23 state/provinces cover gender identity in bias statutes.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Reporting an incident may force document disclosure under the national regime.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Outcome of the due-process suit and the 16 June 2026 narrowing are unknown; no enforcement record under the division law yet, so its practical application is unresolved; custody placement for visitors unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: An active legal challenge exists and courts have blocked some national measures.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unresolved litigation cannot be credited as relief; the operative rule on the books is the criminal statute.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.25-D has a birth-sex facility rule plus recurrent police stops but no facility crime. This division goes further: criminal penalty reaching private businesses, plus a more hostile national document regime. Rates at or slightly below 0.25-D; I place it just above 0.25 because no visitor arrests under the new law are yet documented and some national measures are enjoined.

0.35-A is a birth-sex rule with court-upheld exclusions but no criminal offence. This jurisdiction is materially worse: a criminal statute with jail exposure, national document restrictions, documented custody abuse, and foreign travel advisories. Above 0.35-A's peers would be wrong; this sits below it.

0.15-E features arrest on sight, weeks-long detention and routine extortion. This jurisdiction lacks documented sweeps or on-sight arrest campaigns; enforcement of the bathroom offence has no recorded cases. Hence materially above the 0.15 tier despite comparable legal hostility on paper.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces two stacked exposures. First, a tier-1 universal measure: the division's bathroom crime covers every public-facing business, so an outed or outable visitor carries criminal exposure in daily life, with the challenge unresolved and no working remedy on the record. Second, the national layer converts discovery at the border into refusal, fraud findings with lifetime ineligibility, or custody placement in a corrections system documented to strip hormones and tolerate abuse. Minor-travelling guardians face state-mandated disclosure plus national facilitation prosecutions. Mitigants — partial state protections, enjoined orders, pending litigation, no documented sweeps — lower but do not neutralise this: the harshest operative rule (criminalised facilities plus birth-sex documents) is in force. High-risk band, near its lower boundary.
